processes.name: Airflow scheduler
processes.description: A scheduler that runs in the landing network, lists and reads files from the landing bucket, and triggers a Spark transform job.
processes.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.

processes.name: Spark transform job
processes.description: A Spark job that normalizes records and loads them into BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket where insurance partners place daily extract files containing claim records with member names and dates of birth.
data_stores.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted" and that it is on defaults as far as the speaker knows.

data_stores.name: Airflow metadata database
data_stores.description: Airflow's metadata database, which stores its connection strings and partner keys.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I don't know ... whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest" and that it is on defaults as far as the speaker knows.

data_stores.name: BigQuery
data_stores.description: The warehouse into which the Spark transform job loads normalized claim records and which analysts query directly.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
data_stores.notes: The warehouse grant is dataset-wide and member-identifying columns have not been split out.

assumptions.assumption: The insurance partner file transfer provides encryption in transit because it uses SFTP.
assumptions.basis: The source states that partners push files over SFTP; SFTP is an encrypted file-transfer protocol.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow scheduler presents a non-web interface because it is described as a scheduler that runs a scheduled batch process.
assumptions.basis: The source describes an Airflow scheduler that wakes at 02:00 and processes files, which supports classifying it as non-web.

assumptions.assumption: The Spark transform job presents a non-web interface because it is described as a transform job rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a Spark transform job that normalizes records and loads them into BigQuery, which supports classifying it as non-web.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contains confidential data because the extracts contain member names, dates of birth, and claim records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow metadata database contains confidential data because it stores connection strings and partner keys.
assumptions.basis: The source states that Airflow keeps its connection strings and partner keys in the metadata database.

assumptions.assumption: BigQuery contains confidential data because it stores normalized claim records with member names and dates of birth.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth and that the transformed records are loaded into BigQuery.
